claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT can reveal a ferromagnetic ground state by computing total-energy differences between competing magnetic configurations.
DFT+U corrections may be needed for some materials.
The proposed calculations represent a 0 K bulk system under periodic boundary conditions.
The electron-density distribution mediates stabilization of ferromagnetic ordering.
Exchange splitting mediates stabilization of ferromagnetic ordering.
Spin-polarized DFT explicitly treats spin degrees of freedom.
Spin-polarized DFT permits total energies to be calculated for different magnetic states.
A ferromagnetic state is identified as the ground state when its calculated total energy is lower than those of the non-magnetic and antiferromagnetic states.
A lower energy of the ferromagnetic state indicates that exchange interactions favor parallel spin alignment.
The ferromagnetic configuration is predicted to have lower total energy than the non-magnetic and antiferromagnetic configurations.
Calculated magnetic moments are predicted to be consistent with ferromagnetic order.
The approach is most reliable when electron correlation is moderately well described by DFT.
Strongly correlated materials may require methods beyond standard DFT, such as DFT+DMFT.
Prediction accuracy depends on the chosen exchange-correlation functional.
Prediction accuracy depends on how electron correlation is treated.
The hypothesis is falsified if the ferromagnetic configuration does not have the lowest calculated total energy under the common DFT setup.
The claimed predictive accuracy is falsified if calculated magnetic moments differ significantly from experimental measurements.
